cleanIntro: The Model 41 field strips without tools and without a trigger pull: magazine out, slide locked open, the trigger guard swings down and the barrel lifts straight off the top, then the slide comes back, up and forward off the frame with its recoil spring and rod. Smith & Wesson stops there and forbids anything further. The two things this pistol will not forgive are a dry-fire snap, which the book says damages it, and a pistol tipped over while the trigger guard is down, which drops the barrel.

steps.title: Muzzle safe, finger off, trigger forward
steps.action: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Keep your finger off the trigger and outside the trigger guard, and check the trigger is in its at-rest, forward position before you start.
steps.prose: The book begins the strip with the trigger forward and never asks you to pull it, and that matters on this pistol: Smith & Wesson warns that dry firing the Model 41 damages it. Nothing in this guide calls for a trigger pull, so if your hand is drifting to it, stop.
steps.quote: Point the pistol in a safe direction. Make sure your finger is off the trigger, and the trigger is in the “at rest” or forward position.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23
steps.warn: WARNING: DO NOT DRY FIRE THE MODEL 41 PISTOL, AS DAMAGE TO THE PISTOL MAY RESULT.

steps.title: Magazine out
steps.action: Press the magazine release and take the magazine out of the pistol, finger still off the trigger and out of the guard.
steps.prose: The Model 41 has a magazine disconnect safety, which blocks the trigger linkage with the magazine out, but it is no substitute for clearing the chamber. Smith & Wesson's warning is specific: a finger on the trigger while the magazine comes out can fire the pistol.
steps.quote: Depress the magazine release, and remove the magazine from the pistol.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23
steps.warn: NEVER PLACE YOUR FINGER ON THE TRIGGER OR IN THE TRIGGER GUARD WHILE YOU REMOVE THE MAGAZINE. DOING SO COULD CAUSE THE HANDGUN TO FIRE.

steps.title: Slide back hard, then lock it open
steps.action: Hold the pistol upright, grasp the serrated sides of the slide from the rear with thumb and fingers, and draw it briskly all the way back to extract any cartridge from the chamber. Then press the slide stop lever up so the slide stays locked open.
steps.prose: Brisk is the word that matters: a slow pull can leave a .22 rim hanging on the extractor instead of throwing it clear. Keep your hand away from the ejection port so nothing blocks the round on its way out. The slide has to stay locked open for the next steps.
steps.quote: briskly draw the slide fully rearward in order to extract any cartridge from the barrel chamber and clear it from the pistol. Lock the slide into the open position by pressing the slide stop lever to the up position.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23

steps.title: Look in the chamber and at the breech face
steps.action: Look into the chamber and down through the magazine well and make certain both are empty. While the slide is open, look at the breech face: the firing pin must not be sticking out of it.
steps.prose: A protruding firing pin is the one finding in this book that stops everything. Smith & Wesson's instruction is to unload the pistol and have it inspected and test-fired by a gunsmith qualified on Smith & Wesson firearms before it is used again.
steps.quote: Make certain that the chamber is empty.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23
steps.warn: WARNING: VERIFY THAT THE FIRING PIN IS NOT PROTRUDING FROM THE BREECH FACE. IF THE FIRING PIN IS PROTRUDING, MAKE SURE THE FIREARM IS POINTED IN A SAFE DIRECTION, UNLOAD THE FIREARM AND HAVE IT INSPECTED AND TEST FIRED BY A GUNSMITH QUALIFIED TO PERFORM SERVICE ON SMITH & WESSON FIREARMS.

steps.title: Trigger guard down
steps.action: Hold the pistol in your shooting hand, slide still locked open, and rotate the trigger guard downward. It is the latch that holds the barrel on.
steps.prose: The trigger guard pivots at its front; you are swinging its rear down, away from the frame. Do not touch the trigger while the guard is down.
steps.quote: While holding the pistol in the shooting hand, rotate the trigger guard down
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23

steps.title: Keep it upright, lift the barrel off
steps.action: Keep the pistol upright and lift the barrel assembly straight up and off the frame.
steps.prose: With the trigger guard down nothing holds the barrel, and if the pistol is tipped over it falls off on its own. That is the mistake this step invites: a dropped barrel lands on its muzzle or its sights, and the Model 41 is a target pistol whose accuracy lives in both.
steps.quote: Make sure the pistol remains upright so that the barrel assembly will not fall off when released, lift off barrel assembly
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23

steps.title: Slide back and up
steps.action: With the barrel off, push the slide back and raise it slightly off the frame, keeping hold of it.
steps.prose: The recoil spring is still under load inside the slide. Keep a firm hand over the slide and spring throughout; the book warns they can fly off and cause injury if you let go.
steps.quote: Push back on the slide and raise it slightly
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.23
steps.warn: WARNING: YOU MUST CONTROL THE SLIDE AND THE SPRING DURING REMOVAL, TO KEEP THEM FROM FLYING OFF AND CAUSING INJURY.

steps.title: Slide forward, off the frame
steps.action: Move the slide assembly forward until it comes free of the frame.
steps.prose: Back, up, then forward: the slide only clears its tracks in that order. If it binds, go back a step rather than forcing it.
steps.quote: Move the slide assembly forward to complete disengagement
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Recoil spring and rod out of the slide
steps.action: Take the recoil spring and the recoil spring rod out of the slide.
steps.prose: Ease them out under your thumb rather than letting the spring jump. Keep the rod and spring together; they go back in as a pair.
steps.quote: Remove recoil spring and recoil spring rod from slide.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.24

steps.title: Field strip complete
steps.action: Five pieces: the barrel, the slide, the recoil spring guide rod, the recoil spring and the frame assembly. Smith & Wesson forbids taking the pistol any further than this.
steps.prose: This is everything the book publishes. From here the bore, the chamber, the slide and the frame are all reachable for cleaning, and the magazine is cleaned whole. Do not dry-fire the frame while the pistol is apart; the book says it will damage it.
steps.quote: NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE DISASSEMBLY/FIELD STRIPPING PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL, OR PERFORM ANY MAINTENANCE, ADJUSTMENT, OR SERVICE NOT SPECIFIED.
steps.cite:
Safety & Instruction Manual
For The Model 41 Pistol
Performance Center ® Models Included — Model_41-REV: 121724 — Field Stripping/Disassembly, p.22
steps.warn: WARNING: NEVER DRY-FIRE YOUR PISTOL IN ITS DISASSEMBLED STATE. DAMAGE TO THE PISTOL WILL RESULT.

deepAbsentReason: Smith & Wesson's Model 41 book ends at the field strip (pages 22 to 24) and forbids going further: its warning on page 22 reads "NEVER DISASSEMBLE YOUR FIREARM BEYOND THE DISASSEMBLY/FIELD STRIPPING PROCEDURE DETAILED IN THIS MANUAL". The magazine is cleaned whole, without being taken apart (page 26), and the trigger stop on page 27 is an adjustment, not a cleaning procedure, so the book has no deeper lane to publish.

cleaning.name: BORE & CHAMBER
tasks: Before the first use, wipe the factory preservative or oil out of the bore and chamber with a clean swab or patch
Brass brush dipped in gun-cleaning solvent through the bore and chamber to lift the firing residue
Finish with a dry cotton patch through the bore to take out the residue and the solvent
If spent cases are hard to extract, clean the chamber thoroughly with solvent; if it keeps happening, change ammunition brand

cleaning.name: SLIDE & FRAME
tasks: Wipe the exterior with a non-abrasive cleaning cloth
After cleaning, lightly coat the metal parts, inside and out, with a good gun oil
Wipe off cleaning solution, oil and fingerprints: moisture from your fingers left on the steel can start corrosion
Do not use ammoniated or other strong alkaline solvents on any Smith & Wesson firearm
Do not leave the pistol soaking in solvent or in an ultrasonic cleaner for long; it can damage the finish

cleaning.name: LUBRICATION
tasks: One drop of firearms lubricant at each of the two lubrication points the manual's lubrication figure shows
Do not over-lubricate: excess oil gathers unburned powder and carbon that can stop the pistol working properly
In a cold climate, use an oil weight that will not congeal
After exposure to sand, dust, heavy humidity or water, clean and lubricate before the pistol is used again

cleaning.name: MAGAZINE
tasks: Wipe every exposed surface of the magazine with a clean cloth
Wipe the top of the follower and the inside of the magazine lips
Hold the follower down with the load assist button and swab the inside of the magazine
Never put lubricant or cleaner directly on ammunition: a contaminated round can squib and leave a bullet lodged in the bore

cleaning.name: STORAGE
tasks: For long storage, oil the bore, chamber and internal mechanism, and coat the external mechanism and barrel with an anti-rust oil
Do not store it in leather or heavy cloth, or with a plug in the barrel: both hold moisture
Clean it again before it is next used
⚠ Check for wear every time you clean; if the wear is excessive, stop using it and return it to Smith & Wesson or a qualified gunsmith

reassembly: Fit the recoil spring rod into the recoil spring, then put the spring and rod into the slide.
Put the slide and recoil spring assembly onto the frame, with the recoil spring lined up in its space in the frame.
Pull the slide back as far as it will go so its rails engage the tracks in the frame.
Lock the slide open: let it come forward slightly while you push up on the slide stop.
Place the barrel onto the frame and slide and push it down into place.
Rotate the trigger guard up into place against the frame.
⛔ Do not snap the trigger to test the reassembly: Smith & Wesson warns that dry firing damages the Model 41.
fncheck: With the pistol empty and pointed in a safe direction, work the slide: Smith & Wesson's inspection asks that it moves freely along the frame through its full length of travel, and that the firing pin is not protruding from the breech face. A protruding firing pin means the pistol goes to a gunsmith qualified on Smith & Wesson firearms before it is fired. The book publishes no trigger-pull test and warns that dry firing damages the Model 41, so do not pull the trigger to check your work.
